title: The Object class
context: What methods does every Java object inherit from Object, and what should you know about them?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java basics questions (2 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Every class extends `Object`, directly or indirectly. Its main methods are `equals` (identity by default), `hashCode` (an int consistent with equals), `toString` (a text form, default ClassName@hash), `getClass`, `clone` (protected, a shallow copy only if the class implements Cloneable), `wait`, `notify` and `notifyAll` (for monitors), and `finalize` (deprecated, don't rely on it). Override equals and hashCode together, and toString for useful logs.

points.title: equals and hashCode pair
points.why: Hash-based collections depend on both methods agreeing.

points.title: finalize is deprecated
points.why: Finalizers run late or never. Use try-with-resources or Cleaner instead.
